firmographic.name: Mercury
firmographic.company_description:
Mercury Technologies, Inc. is a San Francisco-based, privately held fintech founded in 2017 by Immad Akhund that provides a software-first digital banking and financial operations platform targeted primarily at startups, small businesses, and ecommerce brands. Its core offering is a free business checking and savings account with no monthly fees, $0 ACH and domestic/USD international wires, debit cards, and up to $5M of FDIC insurance delivered through a sweep network of partner banks (Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., Evolve Bank & Trust). The platform extends modularly into treasury management (Mercury Treasury via JPM and Morgan Stanley funds, up to 3.61% net yield), lending (Mercury IO Mastercard via Patriot Bank; Mercury Venture Debt and Mercury Working Capital Loans originated by Mercury Lending, LLC), payments and invoicing, expense management, and accounting automations synced to QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite. A developer-facing Mercury API plus open-source CLI and Mercury MCP server extend programmatic banking to AI agents and integrations.

Mercury's business model blends float-related revenue, subscriptions, and transaction fees. Treasury yield spread on idle cash (0.15%–0.60% monthly fee on Treasury balances), subscription revenue from Mercury Plus ($29.90/mo) and Mercury Pro ($299/mo), and Mercury Personal ($240/yr, waived for eligible business users) anchor recurring income, while card interchange, Mercury Lending interest and origination fees, FX fees (1% on non-USD wires), 1099 filing fees, and Mercury Invest advisory fees (0.10% AUM) contribute transactional revenue. Distribution is product-led and self-serve via mercury.com with a ~10-minute online onboarding, complemented by an inside-sales motion for Pro and $10M+ accounts, high-touch Treasury Solutions for $25M+ balances via Morgan Stanley, and a developer/AI-agent channel through the public API, CLI, and MCP server.

The company reached $650M in annualized revenue as of Q3 2025 (up from $500M at end-2024) on a customer base exceeding 300,000 — approximately one in three U.S. startups — with four consecutive years of GAAP and EBITDA profitability. Mercury received conditional OCC approval in April 2026 to establish Mercury Bank, N.A. in Utah, completed a $200M Series D led by TCV at a $5.2B valuation in May 2026, and launched Mercury Command, an AI conversational financial operator, in June 2026. Strategic acquisitions of Teal (accounting infrastructure, 2024) and Central (AI-native payroll, 2026) extend the platform into adjacent workflows, while Mercury Personal and Mercury MCP indicate expansion into consumer banking and AI-agent-native banking infrastructure.

recent_move.description: Received conditional OCC approval to establish Mercury Bank, N.A. as a nationally chartered bank in Utah, a strategic shift from the partner-bank model toward owning payment rails and unlocking Zelle, expanded lending, and direct federal supervision (pending FDIC and Federal Reserve approvals).

Closed a $200M Series D led by TCV at a $5.2B post-money valuation (~49% step-up over the March 2025 Series C), with participation from a16z, Coatue, CRV, Sapphire Ventures, Sequoia, and Spark Capital to fund the bank charter push and AI product development.

Launched Mercury Command, an AI conversational financial operator embedded in Mercury accounts that executes multi-step tasks (payments, invoicing, card management, transaction categorization, auto-transfer rules) via natural language with explicit user approval.

Acquired Central, an AI-native payroll platform serving nearly 500 customers and processing over $175M in payroll, extending the platform into payroll and consolidating adjacent workflows for startups.

Launched Mercury Personal, a premium consumer banking product ($240/year, waived for eligible business users) with 3.25% APY savings, Mercury Invest ETF portfolios, and Mercury Command for personal accounts, expanding into a new customer segment adjacent to the business core.
Acquired Teal, a Vancouver-based seed-stage accounting infrastructure startup ($8M raised led by Torch Capital), to deepen in-product accounting capabilities and vertical-software integration.

Mercury Technologies Inc. applied for a national bank charter with the OCC and deposit insurance with the FDIC, with Mercury Bank N.A. proposed as a wholly owned subsidiary headquartered in Utah. The move shifts Mercury from a partner-bank model toward operating as a fully chartered national bank.

leadership_change.title: Appointment of Jon Auxier as CEO of Mercury Bank

expansion_highlight.description: Conditional OCC approval (April 2026) for Mercury Bank, N.A. and the appointment of Jon Auxier (formerly CFO of SoFi Bank) as the subsidiary's CEO indicate a structural shift from a BaaS/partner-bank model to direct ownership of payment rails, unlocking Zelle, expanded lending, and direct Fed/OCC supervision.

Launch of Mercury Personal in December 2025 introduces a new consumer-banking segment ($240/year subscription, waived for eligible business users), extending the customer base from businesses to founders and individuals and creating a self-serve upsell path.

Acquisition of Central (AI-native payroll, April 2026) and Teal (accounting infrastructure, September 2024) signal continued in-house buildout of payroll and accounting product lines adjacent to core banking, reducing reliance on third-party integrations.

Mercury MCP server (AI-agent-ready Model Context Protocol), open-source CLI on GitHub, and full banking API/SDK with sandbox reflect expansion into a developer- and AI-agent-facing distribution channel, targeting programmable banking as a distinct go-to-market surface.

Reported expansion beyond AI/tech startups into ecommerce, agencies, VC funds, crypto, accounting firms, LLCs, life science, climate, real estate and construction, and healthcare services — with 73% of new customers coming from outside the AI/tech category — indicates active vertical broadening beyond the original ICP.

$200M Series D in May 2026 at a $5.2B valuation, with TCV leading and broad participation from existing top-tier investors, signals continued investor confidence and capital availability to fund the bank charter, AI development, and product expansion.

TrevorWorks-style dedicated inside-sales motion for Pro subscribers and accounts with $10M+ balance, plus high-touch Treasury Solutions via Morgan Stanley for $25M+ balances, signal mid-market and enterprise upmarket expansion.
